subject: Risk & Compliance
title: PCI DSS for Payment Security
description: A micro-lesson that makes PCI DSS for Payment Security usable.

hook.text: Every business taking credit cards must follow PCI DSS rules. Break them, and you lose the right to process payments.

buildup.text: PCI DSS sets 12 requirements for protecting cardholder data — from encryption to access controls.

discovery.text: Created in 2004 by Visa and Mastercard, it's enforced through fines and the threat of losing card processing.

twist.text: Most breaches happen at companies that were PCI compliant on paper but not in practice.

climax.text: Compliance isn't security. Checking a box doesn't mean the controls actually work under attack.

punchline.text: Compliant on paper. Breached in practice. Every time.

quiz.question: What happens if a business violates PCI DSS?
options: Fines and potential loss of ability to process cards
